title: Hysteresis-based Region Decider for Tiered Routing using p50/p95 Telemetry and Link Health Scores
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Region selection currently flips too quickly when percentile latency spikes or transient packet loss occurs. This causes client-visible tail latency regressions and higher cost due to unnecessary model variant fallbacks. Goal: Implement a hysteresis-aware region decider that uses p50 and p95 latency windows plus a lightweight network-health score (combining packet loss, TCP retransmit spikes, and error-rate) to make stable tier routing and fallback decisions. The decider should bias toward the configured preferred region unless telemetry indicates sustained degradation, support per-customer tier overrides, and expose debug metadata for Console and logs. Constraints: must be cheap in realtime (O(1) per request), compatible with existing routing policy config, support rollout via canary flags, and maintain existing SLA for hosted API customers.
design_notes: Architecture: 1) Rolling metrics layer computes sliding-window percentiles for p50 and p95 at 30s and 5m windows, plus a normalized Network Health Score (0-100) computed from packet loss percentage, connection error rate, and inter-PoP latency variance. 2) Decision logic: prefer region if (p95_30s < prefer_threshold) AND (HealthScore_30s > min_health) OR if p50_30s shows stable improvement for hysteresis_duration. 3) Hysteresis: use two thresholds (enter/exit) for p95 and HealthScore to avoid flip-flop. 4) Cooldown: once a region switch occurs, enforce a cooldown window (default 3m) before allowing another switch unless degradation is severe. 5) Tier routing: map customer tiers to preferred thresholds (e.g., P0/P1: aggressive failover at lower p95, P2/P3: higher tolerance). 6) Fallback model variants: attach variant map that indicates compatible fallback models ranked by cost and latency; if network health is poor but p95 is OK, prefer lighter variants rather than cross-region failover. Implementation notes: implement decider as a stateless policy with external quick state store for hysteresis flags (Redis TTL keyed by deployment-region-customer). Decision API returns chosen region, chosen variant, reasoning tags, and diagnostic sample of the recent percentiles.
telemetry_queries: 1) p50/p95 aggregation: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 50) AS p50_30s, percentile(latency_ms,95) AS p95_30s FROM request_latencies WHERE region = :region AND ts > now() - 30s GROUP BY region. 2) 5m window: same query with 5m. 3) Network health: compute packet_loss = sum(dropped)/sum(sent), conn_errors = sum(conn_errors)/sum(connections), retransmits = percentile(retransmits,95). Normalize: HealthScore = 100 - clamp( weight1*packet_loss_pct + weight2*conn_errors_pct + weight3*(retransmits_norm), 0,100 ). 4) Error-rate: SELECT sum(status >= 500)/count(*) over 30s. 5) Anomaly detection: rolling z-score on p95 to detect sudden spikes. 6) Dashboarding: expose per-region p50/p95, HealthScore, switching events counter, cooldown active gauge.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Decision service produces stable region choices under synthetic bursty latency tests (no more than 1 switch per 5m under controlled jitter). 2) For a simulated regional outage (packet loss > 5% sustained for 2m), traffic is moved to fallback region within the configured SLO for P1 customers and within cooldown logic for P2. 3) Hysteresis prevents oscillation for brief spikes (p95 spike < duration threshold). 4) Console shows debugging tags for the routed requests and exposes switch events and counts. 5) Integration tests covering tier overrides and variant selection pass in CI. 6) End-to-end Canary release shows <=5% increase in error-rate and no customer-visible latency regressions for 24h before full rollout.
rollout_steps: 1) Merge decider behind feature flag and run closed canary in staging with synthetic traffic. 2) Enable for internal services in prod with traffic mirror for 24h and monitor switch count. 3) Canary cohort: enable for 1% of traffic for non-critical tenants for 72h and evaluate metrics. 4) Gradual ramp by 10% every 12h with automated rollback if switch_rate or error_rate exceed thresholds. 5) Enable per-customer tier configs and monitor customer-impact dashboard. 6) Full enable for hosted API after two successful 24h canaries and PM sign-off.
test_plan: Unit tests for threshold math and hysteresis state transitions. Integration tests that simulate: transient p95 spikes, sustained p95 degradation, packet loss bursts, and combined scenarios. Load test with traffic patterns from 10 customers across three regions to validate CPU/memory overhead. Chaos test: randomly drop 1/3 of telemetry points and assert decision stability. Add smoke tests that validate variant selection mapping for model families. Post-deploy: run 48h runbook that checks switch_count, mean p95, HealthScore trends, and customer error-rate.
risks: 1) Incorrect threshold tuning may cause unnecessary cross-region failovers increasing cost and degrading cold-cache latencies. 2) Dependence on telemetry freshness — delayed metrics could trigger late switches. 3) State-store (Redis) availability affecting hysteresis flags. 4) Complex tier mappings could be misconfigured causing inconsistent behavior across customers. Mitigations: conservative defaults, traffic mirroring, graceful fallback to static priority list, and dashboards with alerting thresholds.
